## 1. The question I selected

The opening came from the independent algebra attack, drawing on Astra’s N1137 approach to exact counting and uniform generation.

A chain complex consists of matrices

\[
R^{n_L}\xrightarrow{d_L}R^{n_{L-1}}
\longrightarrow\cdots
\xrightarrow{d_2}R^{n_1}\xrightarrow{d_1}R^{n_0}
\]

satisfying all the coupled equations

\[
d_i d_{i+1}=0.
\]

These matrices encode boundaries and homology. The compatibility condition is global: choosing or correcting one matrix affects the constraints on its neighbours.

I asked:

> **Can we construct exact generative coordinates for every such tuple over a finite local ring, retaining the multiplicities needed for uniform sampling, and determine the entire dependence on arithmetic depth?**

The selected ring class is **finite commutative chain rings**: rings whose ideals form one chain, with maximal ideal generated by a uniformizer \(\pi\). Two examples are

\[
\mathbb F_q[t]/(t^e)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb Z/p^e\mathbb Z.
\]

The first has polynomial coefficients and truncation; the second has integer carries. They can have the same residue field and length while having different arithmetic.

The construction resolves this question for all finite commutative chain rings with explicit arithmetic interfaces.

| Operation | Established result |
|---|---|
| Count | Exact number of all actual matrix tuples satisfying every adjacent-product constraint |
| Generate | Exact uniform sampling of those tuples |
| Convert | Deterministic, reversible conversion between ring families with the same identified residue field and length |
| Evaluate all depths | A finite integer transfer matrix and explicit rational generating function |
| Determine growth | Exact exponential rate, polynomial correction and positive leading constants |
| Describe typical deep reductions | Explicit limiting path weights, geometric residence counts and a Dirichlet law |

The objects counted are **actual matrices in fixed coordinates**. Changes of basis are used internally, with their multiplicities retained.

## 7. What was executed, and what the costs cover

The implementation includes:

- exact counting and actual-entry sampling over \(\mathbb F_p[t]/(t^e)\);
- an independent integer-ring implementation over \(\mathbb Z/p^e\mathbb Z\);
- the deterministic conversion and inverse between those two families;
- the finite transfer evaluator and symbolic generating function;
- the growth optimizer;
- a positive rational evaluator for the leading constants, requiring no enumeration of strict paths.

The principal checks were:

| Verification | Executed scope |
|---|---:|
| Exhaustive actual-tuple counts over truncated polynomial rings | 11 fixtures |
| Exhaustive actual-tuple counts over integer residue rings | 11 fixtures |
| Complete gauge-coordinate bijections and inverses | 9 fibers |
| Actual cross-ring conversions and inverse recovery | Every one of 4,349 complexes across five fixtures |
| Transfer matrix against the depth recurrence | 1,768 equalities |
| Symbolic generating functions, pole orders and leading constants | 8 fixtures |
| Growth optimizer against full reachable-state optimization | 1,092 dimension vectors |
| Independent scalar valuation formula | 120 comparisons |
| All-depth one-step lifting probabilities | 6 exhaustive fixtures |

There are also larger generated examples and a mixed-characteristic check at \(p=2^{61}-1\), using arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic.

For dimensions \((2,3,4,3,2)\), residue field \(\mathbb F_2\), and depth eight, the program counted approximately \(5.9\times10^{50}\) valid complexes inside an ambient space of \(2^{288}\) tuples. The transfer matrix has 76 states. Actual matrices were generated over both ring families, and every adjacent product was checked in its actual ring.

Those are correctness demonstrations. No comparative performance advantage over equally informed specialist software is claimed.

### Complexity boundaries

For a fixed number \(s=L+1\) of grades, the counting recurrence uses at most

\[
(\lceil e/2\rceil+1)\prod_i(n_i+1)
\]

states and

\[
O\!\left((e+1)(N+1)^{2s-1}\right)
\]

transitions. Integer bit lengths and arithmetic costs are retained, giving polynomial bit complexity in the explicit parameters for fixed \(s\).
